# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 65 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 48 | Coptic

---

## Saying 65

He said: "There was a decent man who owned a vineyard. He leased it to some tenant farmers to work it, in exchange for a share of the harvest. He sent his servant to collect the owner's share. The farmers grabbed the servant, beat him nearly to death, and sent him away. The servant went back and reported this. The owner thought: 'Maybe they didn't know who he was.' So he sent another servant. They beat that one too. Then the owner sent his own son, thinking: 'Surely they'll respect my son.' But when the farmers saw that the son was the heir, they seized him and killed him. If you have ears, use them."

---

**Translator's Notes (PNEUMA):**

- "Decent man" — *agathos* as ordinary moral goodness, not grandiosity
- "In exchange for a share of the harvest" — the sharecropping arrangement made clear
- "If you have ears, use them" — fresh rendering of the closing formula
- The naivety of the owner is heightened by "Surely they'll respect my son"
